note: Quantities the manuscript cites that are derived from the pipeline but appear inside no results/ file. Regenerate with `make facts`. atlas.check_manuscript_numbers compares the manuscript's stated guardrail count against guardrail_tests_collected rather than looking it up in the value pool: both 102 and 118 -- the counts this manuscript carried before -- match exactly one unrelated pipeline value each, so a stale count would be reported as verified. How many tests PASS depends on the checkout (a release archive ships data/ and results/, a git archive does not), so the passing count must be measured from the release at release time.
archive_measured_for_version: working tree after v2.4.0 with the default-matrix fix and its 11 regression tests, measured as a reader sees it: the submission-package checks need the author's own deliverables and skip without them, so the count does not depend on whose machine runs it. Measured with HOME pointed at an empty directory: 158 passed, 23 skipped. On the day of measurement Ensembl REST returned 503, so its one live-service test skipped too and the run reported 157 passed, 24 skipped; the recorded figures are with that service up. On the author's machine the same extract additionally runs the package checks and gives 178 passed, 1 failed and 2 skipped, the failure being the deferred guardrail count in the cover letter, and that difference is the reason the reader's figure is the one recorded
bare_clone_measured_for: a fresh clone of the working tree after v2.4.0 with the default-matrix fix; results/, data/ and the package absent
